standard_prerequisites.name: Left duals and the adjunction with the tensor product
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Categories, Lemma categories-lemma-left-dual and Remark categories-remark-left-dual-adjoint
standard_prerequisites.use: Supply the identification of Hom(X tensor Y, Z) with Hom(X, Z tensor Y) and the criterion for an object to be a left dual of another, which the proof uses throughout.

standard_prerequisites.name: Karoubian categories and split idempotents
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies that an idempotent endomorphism of an object produces a direct sum decomposition, applied to the idempotents obtained in the endomorphism algebra of the dual.

core_obligations: The endomorphism algebras (proof lines 4223-4238): using the adjunction, the author identifies Hom(X, X) with Hom(1, X tensor Y) and with Hom(Y, Y), and shows that under this bijection precomposition by an endomorphism of X corresponds to postcomposition by the corresponding endomorphism of Y; hence the bijection is an isomorphism from the opposite of the algebra Hom(X, X) to the algebra Hom(Y, Y).

Splitting the idempotents (proof lines 4238-4244): for a direct sum decomposition X = X_1 + X_2 the two projectors correspond to idempotents in Hom(Y, Y), so Karoubian-ness provides a decomposition Y = Y_1 + Y_2; the identification Hom(Z' tensor X, Z) = Hom(Z', Z tensor Y) then restricts to identifications Hom(Z' tensor X_i, Z) = Hom(Z', Z tensor Y_i) for i = 1, 2, functorially in Z' and Z.
Conclusion (proof lines 4244-4247): the restricted identifications exhibit Y_i as a left dual of X_i by the cited criterion.
proof_roadmap: Identify the endomorphism algebras of an object and of its left dual as opposite algebras.
Transport the idempotents given by a direct sum decomposition through that isomorphism.
Use the restricted identifications to exhibit the summands of the dual as duals of the summands.
difficulty_reason: The lemma states that in a Karoubian additive monoidal category every direct summand of an object admitting a left dual again admits a left dual (statement lines 4216-4220). The proof is a complete argument: the adjunction identifies the endomorphism algebra of the object with the algebra of its dual and shows that the identification reverses composition (proof lines 4223-4238); the idempotents coming from a direct sum decomposition are transported to the dual, where Karoubian-ness splits them, and the adjunction restricts to the pieces (proof lines 4238-4244); the resulting identifications give the required duals of the summands (proof lines 4244-4247). The non-formal content is the transport of idempotents through the algebra anti-isomorphism. The claim is H2: a structured argument with each input named.
